items.headline: AMD's Lisa Su keynote turns the MI400 roadmap into shipping product
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday the story was anticipation: the floor opened at Moscone West while the MI450/Helios reveal and the customer roster stayed held for Thursday's keynote, with the stock near $553, pre-event reporting pegging OpenAI and Meta at a combined 12 gigawatts, and Helios racks only rumored around $5 to $5.5 million. Today the keynote landed and converted roadmap into product: Su detailed the Instinct MI400 family, put the flagship MI455X at 432GB of HBM4 and up to 34x the token throughput of the MI355X, and declared Helios 'in full production' with third-quarter shipments ramping through the second half of 2027. The pre-event 'combined 12GW' framing resolved into named capacity, and Anthropic surfaced as a newly named buyer at 2 gigawatts alongside OpenAI at 6 (already taking pre-production racks), plus a deepened Meta tie and AT&T at roughly a trillion tokens a month. The one number that never reached a slide was a Helios list price, so the rack-versus-Vera-Rubin case now rests on the 30%-more-tokens-per-dollar claim, and the open question shifts from whether the keynote would deliver to whether the second-half shipment ramp holds.

items.headline: White House accuses Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic's Fable to build Kimi K3
items.diff_narrative: A storyline with no antecedent in yesterday's report. Michael Kratsios, the White House OSTP director, accused Beijing-based Moonshot AI of building its 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 by running large-scale distillation against Anthropic's Fable, and of training on Nvidia GB300 servers reached 'through Thailand' to skirt export controls, fusing model-weight provenance and chip-export enforcement into a single charge days before Moonshot's planned weight release. The accusation drew immediate pushback: the Laude Institute's Braden Hancock noted Fable had only been public since July 1, leaving no realistic window to distill and ship a frontier-class model in two weeks, while the Allen Institute's Nathan Lambert argued supervised distillation loses its edge as Chinese models near the frontier. The administration detailed no evidence for how it concluded K3 was distilled from Fable; Anthropic's Sarah Heck backed the White House, Moonshot declined to comment, and a Chinese embassy spokesperson called the allegations 'entirely unfounded.'

items.headline: OpenAI ships Presence, a governance layer for production agents
items.diff_narrative: New today, and a move up the stack from selling model access to selling the machinery that governs an agent in production. Presence bundles written policies and SOPs, guardrails, an allowlist of approved actions, simulations and grader-based evaluations, and the load-bearing control: a requirement that human staff sign off before any behavioral change reaches production, with a Codex-powered improvement loop that re-enters that same gate. OpenAI is its own first reference customer, reporting that Presence resolves about 75% of its English-language inbound support calls without a human, and it ships in limited general availability through the account team and Forward Deployed Engineers rather than self-service. This bullet also carries the only trace of yesterday's headline intrusion, a single clause noting OpenAI's evaluation models breached Hugging Face, used as context for why provable control over agent actions is becoming the thing enterprises pay for; the standalone Hugging Face breach story did not otherwise continue.

items.headline: OpenAI commits to a 3.2-gigawatt Georgia data center (Project Camellia)
items.diff_narrative: New today. OpenAI unveiled Project Camellia, a four-building campus in Effingham County, Georgia, backed by at least $20 billion in private investment and drawing 3.2 gigawatts under a 25-year supply agreement with Georgia Power, with power phased in from 2028 to 2032, first operations targeted for 2028, and broader reporting putting full build-out above $30 billion. OpenAI says it will pay the full cost of the electrical infrastructure to shield existing ratepayers, has offered up to a gigawatt of flexible demand response to steady the regional grid, and committed local education, safety and health funding plus Codex credits for Georgia students. The structural signal is that frontier labs are now signing their own multi-decade utility deals and financing substations directly, because grid interconnection, not GPU supply, has become the binding constraint on frontier-scale compute.

items.headline: AI events to plan around
items.diff_narrative: The standing events roundup carries over with one dating shift: AMD's Advancing AI moves from 'live this week' to closing today, so its keynote catalyst has now passed and the section's nearest fixed deadline becomes the Hot Chips early-registration cutoff on July 31. The August security block (Black Hat, DEF CON with its AI Village, SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit) and the developer and infrastructure track beyond it are otherwise unchanged from yesterday.
